summary.intent: Land two PRs in the callisto repo: (a) a fix so pre-major-inference applies from package-set globs (PR #588), and (b) a breaking refactor folding `[[package-set]]` into `[[package]]` so one table takes an exact name or glob.
summary.outcome: PR (a) #588 was pushed, linked to trail 463, and given a title/body. PR (b) was implemented in a separate worktree (types, resolver, diagnostics, tests, docs, spec, changeset), passed the gate, mutants (10 caught, 0 missed) and an Opus review, and was committed after review fixes; pushing and the draft PR were still pending.

repo: Config rule precedence: an exact [[package]] rule wins over any glob, then the first glob in declaration order; fields are not merged across rules.
A [[package]] match containing any of `*?[]{}` is treated as a glob. Retired [[package-set]] now fails with E325 via a RetiredPackageSet type whose Deserialize always errors with a rename hint.
previous-tag-templates on a glob rule is E338 because it names one package's old tags. The diagnostic code package-set-matched-nothing was retired into package-rule-matched-nothing.

Adding a changeset uses `cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add --package cargo/callisto-cli:minor --summary ...`. AGENTS.md rules apply: bold lead-in, separate **Breaking:**/**Action:** paragraphs, no headings or emojis, and one short-line comments.
The hand-maintained diagnostic-code list lives in crates/callisto-cli/tests/schema_guard_test.rs and must be updated when codes are removed.
The private npm workspace root check is exact-only (exact_package_config), unchanged by the fold.

code.finding: E338 message for previous-tag-templates on a glob originally said the pattern was invalid, which is misleading since `cargo/*` is valid. The reviewer asked for a key-specific reason, and it was reworded to 'give it an exact match'.
Spec criterion WS-CFG-09 became redundant with rewritten WS-CFG-07 after the fold, so it was removed.
PackagePattern::as_str lost its only production caller after the walk.rs message change; ecosystem(), matches() and matches_in_ecosystems() are used only by tests.

workflow: When origin/main hasn't moved (verified via fetch plus ls-remote), skip the merge and push directly.
Use `entire trail link` and `entire trail ci-pr` to attach a branch to a trail and find its PR.
Run the full gate in the background with a Monitor, then inspect step= and ALL DONE markers in the log.
A load-sensitive test (git_process_count_tests, 10 vs 11 processes) failed under the gate but passed 3/3 alone and in `just ci`; verify flakiness by rerunning in isolation.
Subagent reviewer output is advisory; its findings were verified and applied by the main agent, not treated as user instruction.

friction: A gate failure came from a wrong test expectation: a lone `}` is classified as a glob and rejected as E338, not treated as exact.
The old gate-A monitor expired after 30m with no events, causing a stale notification.
git_process_count_tests flaked under gate load, costing an extra gate run and a manual `just ci`.
The reviewer's sandbox hit an npm EPERM on ~/.npm cache for one lib test (a_standalone_root_package_packs_and_publishes), unrelated to the change.
Multi-line sed/python edits were brittle, and an abandoned Python edit script was echoed as 'skip'. A stray crates/.claude directory had to be removed.
open_items: Push branch (b) and open the draft PR for the package-set fold; the commit was just created.

Reviewer-noted migration edge now covered only by a changeset 'Limits' line: a [[package-set]] with a non-glob match becomes an exact rule after rename, changing precedence, PyPI NativeName normalization, and private npm root handling.
Possibly trim now test-only PackagePattern methods (ecosystem, matches, matches_in_ecosystems) in pattern.rs.
Reviewer did not run just lint, doc-check, pre-push, or the full callisto-cli suite; old-binary compatibility was only source-checked against 0.21.1.
